messages:
jordan-cs: Hey team, just got an escalation from a customer (emily-customer) — after renaming a tool in the registry yesterday they suddenly see function calls returning 404 / "tool not found" intermittently. They say calls work sometimes and then fail for a few minutes.

emily-customer: Repro steps I gave them: call the tool by the new name via the hosted API: `POST /v1/call` body: `{
  "tool": "DataEnrichV2",
  "args": {"id": 123}
}`. Response: `{"error":"tool not found","code":404}`. If they retry after ~30s it sometimes succeeds.

jordan-cs: Sounds like a name/alias propagation window. Do we have any TTL/async propagation between registry and edge caches?

kevin-eng: Yes — aliases and name->uuid mapping are cached in the routing layer with a small TTL (default 20s) and we also async push registry deltas. But that TTL shouldn't cause multi-minute flaps. Can you paste headers + full error payload from their failing request?

emily-customer: Full response dump they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
X-Route-Version: v2
{
  "error":"tool not found",
  "detail":"no matching tool for name=DataEnrichV2"
}
```

sarah-ops: Not seeing obvious 5xx or infra issues at the time in cluster logs. However, routing logs show a handful of lookups returning a stale `alias`->`uuid` mapping for the old name `dataenrich` (all-lowercase) and then a fallback attempt using case-sensitive match that fails.

kevin-eng: Aha — is the customer calling with camelcase `DataEnrichV2` but the registry entry is `DataEnrichv2` (lowercase v)? We recently changed name normalization to be case preserving, but some internal backfill jobs still expect casefolded keys. That could produce a mix of mappings across nodes.

jordan-cs: They specifically said they renamed `dataenrich` -> `DataEnrichV2`. Could race between rename + alias propagation produce a split-brain where some routing nodes answer by UUID (old) and others only accept the new exact-case name?

kevin-eng: Yes. Repro locally: I created a rename, then hammered the routing layer. Some edge nodes still had the old casefolded key in cache and their fallback logic does an exact lookup first then a case-insensitive scan which is slower and sometimes skipped under load. When the slow path times out we return 404.

kevin-eng: Quick mitigation for the customer: call using the alias UUID instead of name until we roll a hotfix. Example: `POST /v1/call` `{ "tool_uuid": "t-abc123" , "args": {"id": 123}}` — they confirmed that works reliably.

emily-customer: Using the UUID works, thanks. Will that be safe for production? We prefer stable names rather than UUIDs.

sarah-ops: We'll push a short-lived rollback to the name-normalization change on the routing tier and kick the alias cache refresh job. That should restore consistent behavior within a minute. Also scheduling a full registry backfill to ensure all nodes have canonical name casing.

jordan-cs: Can we add a user-facing note/KB for customers hitting this — repr steps and recommended workarounds? I'll draft one but want engineers to confirm cause.

kevin-eng: Confirmed cause: rename + partial rollout of case-preserving name lookup caused mixed mappings across routing nodes, resulting in intermittent 404s for calls that relied on the new-cased name. Actions: 1) push rollback on routing name lookup config (done), 2) run alias backfill (`/admin/registry/backfill?force=true`), 3) add telemetry to detect case-mismatch misses and auto-fallback to case-insensitive resolution for 10s after a rename, 4) publish KB recommending UUID call as short-term workaround.

ops-bot: Deploy started by sarah-ops: revert-name-normalization v=2026.3.15-rc1. Track: deploy-7890.

sarah-ops: Deploy finished, pushed cache refresh to edges. Emily — can you confirm if they still see the 404s?

emily-customer: Customer confirmed no further 404s in the last 10 minutes. They will switch to UUID for a day while you run backfill. Thanks for the quick help :heart:

jordan-cs: Thanks everyone — I'll publish the KB and follow up once backfill completes. Closing out the escalation for now.
